title: Spending and card benefits
oneLiner: Understand where the money went, and whether your card still fits.
goal: Explain the customer's actual spending pattern from their transactions, and establish whether their current card fits it - including the answer 'yes, keep it'.
triggers: is my card right for me

stages.goal: Find what actually prompted this - usually one specific charge or one higher-than-expected bill. Ask with `quick_replies`: `A charge I do not recognise`, `The bill is higher`, `Just curious`.
stages.exitWhen: The trigger is identified, or they confirm it is general curiosity.

stages.goal: Show the real spend pattern from transactions, with a chart, over a period that makes sense. Then ask the question that decides the whole answer, with `quick_replies`: `It happens every month`, `That was a one-off`. Use the last month that actually finished. A request for the month in progress is answered with the part-month figure, labelled partial.
stages.exitWhen: The pattern has been shown and reacted to.

stages.goal: Explain the specific items that caused the surprise, then hand back with `quick_replies`: `That explains it`, `There is another charge`.
Check the current card's benefits against that actual pattern. Ask what they actually value, with `quick_replies`: `Cashback`, `Travel`, `No annual fee`, `Keep it simple`.
stages.exitWhen: The fit - good or bad - has been stated.

stages.goal: Either recommend a change with the tradeoff, or confirm keeping the current card is correct. Offer `quick_replies` that give staying put equal weight: the card you named, `Keep my current card`, `Think it over`. A completed month is the only basis for this; a part-month total is not a monthly one.
stages.exitWhen: A decision or a keep-current conclusion exists.

mustEstablish: The real spend distribution from transactions, not an impression.
Whether a spike is recurring or a one-off - this decides the whole answer.
What they actually value: simplicity, cashback, travel, or no annual fee.
The annual fee they pay today.
Which period the spending figures cover, and whether that month has finished. A part-month total is not a monthly one and cannot be compared with one.
That the figure called spending is spending. Transfers to the customer's own savings, fund purchases and card-bill payments are separate totals, not part of it.
neverDo: Do not recommend a card change off one unusual month. Ask whether the spike repeats.
Do not present reward rates without the caps and the annual fee. An uncapped-sounding benefit that caps at 750 a month is not uncapped.
Do not treat 'keep your current card' as a failed outcome. It is frequently the right answer and should be said with the same confidence as a recommendation.
Do not quote a benefit you have not read from the catalogue this turn.
Do not print a paise figure as rupees. The transactions are held in minor units, and INR 1,17,724 shown as INR 1,17,72,400 is this journey's recorded failure - it reads as an ordinary large number.
Do not call a month complete before it has ended. On 19 September the last completed month is August; the month in progress is a partial period and is labelled one wherever it is shown.
Do not add transfers to the customer's own savings, fund purchases or card-bill payments into a spending total. The card bill is the same money as the card purchases arriving a second time.

Do not work out the spending that would make a card pay for itself. Chasing a percentage back on money the customer did not have to part with leaves them worse off, and justifying an annual fee is the bank's job.
Do not convert reward points into rupees without a sourced conversion rate. Points stay points; a rupee equivalent built on an assumed redemption value is a claim the product has not made.

objectionPaths.respondBy: Take it at face value and move to getting more from the existing one. Record the objection so it is not raised again.
Then say plainly that no change is warranted, and stop. Do not look for a second reason to switch.

completion.default: The next action is explicit: confirm the current card still fits, prepare a card-change proposal, or save the spend explanation with the surprise accounted for.
completion.nivedita: Keep it to the explanation. Her spending is stable and a card change is rarely warranted - the next action is to confirm no change rather than looking for one.
completion.rhea: Her core journey. The next action is either the card proposal the pattern supports or a clear confirmation that the current card still fits, after separating household and travel spend.
completion.ravi: Visual first - show the chart before the words. He is on a debit card; the next action here is a spend explanation, because a credit product needs his explicit opt-in and belongs in J09.

openers: Where is my money actually going every month?
Is my card still the right one for the way I spend?
Show me what I spent the most on recently
